chapters.title: Chapter 783: The Way Forward
paragraphs: Ling Ran first drew the anatomical structures of Chen Xiaowang’s abdominal cavity on a piece of paper based on the information he had obtained from the Virtual Human along with the examination results.

For surgeons, cholecystectomy was mainly difficult due to the variations in the structures of patients’ cystic artery and bile ducts. The variation was so great that if a person were to categorize humans based on the differences in the structures of their gallbladder arteries and bile ducts, the list might be so long that it could not even fit into a book.
Naturally, Chen Xiaowang’s cystic artery and bile duct varied from those of other humans too.
There was a very obvious abnormality to his cystic artery, as it branched out very early into two arteries. This condition was known as a double cystic artery.

This was considered a very normal abnormality, and tens of thousands of people might exhibit the same abnormality. If the person did not receive surgery related to the gallbladder or bile duct, this abnormality would not be obvious at all. It neither caused any discomfort nor affected a person’s health. It would not even affect the organs around it to a significant extent. It could be said to be even more insignificant than neighborhood committees outside Beijing.
However, if doctors failed to pay attention to this abnormality during cholecystectomy, it could easily lead to problems.

To prevent bleeding, during cholecystectomy, doctors had to first interrupt the blood flow of the cystic artery. As ordinary people only had one cystic artery, doctors just need to clamp their cystic arteries with a hemostatic forceps. However, in cases of patients with double cystic arteries, doctors may make a mistake and only interrupt the blood flow of the first cystic artery. And when this happened, the second cystic artery was almost guaranteed to be accidentally damaged during the process of the surgery. Major hemorrhage was almost a certainty, and a good prognosis would become impossible.
“Double cystic artery!” Ling Ran rose and wrote this down on the whiteboard in his office.
Not only did this serve as a reminder for himself, but also for other doctors to take note of.

Accidental damage sometimes happened because the chief surgeon made a mistake, but there were times when it happened because the chief surgeon did not manage his subordinates well by forgetting to give them a reminder.
“Edema in the gallbladder, and there’s inflammation.”
“The bile duct enters the hepatic duct after running parallel to the hepatic duct for a distance.”
As Ling Ran wrote on the whiteboard, he drew simple diagrams every now and then.
The ability to draw anatomical diagrams were essential to doctors, so it was only natural that other doctors were able to understand what Ling Ran was trying to convey.
Not only did the doctors in the Ling Treatment Group understand it, but doctors from other treatment groups were also sizing up the whiteboard in curiosity.
“Chronic cholecystitis, and the gallbladder has shrunk a little. These aren’t really a problem. The most difficult part is that the patient can only afford a recovery time of two and a half days.”
“I really don’t believe that companies nowadays overwork people to this extent.”

“Employers of companies have to make a living, right? As doctors, even though we are super tired after working day and night, we still carry out freelance surgery during the weekends. Why are we doing all these?”

“Some people chase after money, and some chase after their dreams. Some chase both at the same time. Truth be told, this has nothing to do with us. From what I know, whenever Huawei executes a project, they aim to be two years ahead of their peers. If their employers were to take short breaks, those breaks would accumulate over the course of time into a long period of time. Then, wouldn’t their predecessor’s hard work to race against time become a waste?”
“But they should still have their basic rest time, shouldn’t they?”

“Basic rest time? I don’t know how you were like as a student, but from I know, all the students who abide by the basic rest time either have no problem scoring 985 marks in their college entrance examination at all or can’t even pass after their second try. Which type are you?”
Right after someone talked about school, the doctors’ office in the Emergency Medical Center immediately became a lot livelier.
Huo Congjun slowly walked over to Ling Ran and asked, “Have you made your decision?”
“Yes,” Ling Ran said.

As Huo Congjun looked at the diagrams that Ling Ran drew on the whiteboard, he shook his head and said, “Why would you trouble yourself over this? There are so many patients waiting for you to operate on them. Why don’t you just pass this case over to an ordinary doctor? Moreover, truth be told, isn’t the patient’s request to recover in a span of two and a half days a little too much?”
Ling Ran said, “It’s also an opportunity for self-improvement.”
Huo Congjun asked in surprise, “What do you mean?”

“Improving patients’ prognoses and shortening the recovery time can be seen as an area of improvement when it comes to cholecystectomy.” Ling Ran was actually speculating that this was the way to elevate his cholecystectomy skills from Specialist Level to Master Level.
Unlike the other skills he possessed, Ling Ran learned cholecystectomy from scratch.
Now that he had gone from Novice Level to Specialist Level, Ling Ran did not actually have many ideas as to how to go forward.

Cholecystectomy in itself was a relatively simple surgery, especially when it was done using a laparoscope, and most doctors could complete it without any issue. Even though doctors always strived to reduce damage and improve accuracy, all of this often felt a little vague, and it was not a true indicator of improvements in skills.
Without a doctor who was better at cholecystectomy to guide him, Ling Ran did not know how to improve further.
Without realizing it, Chen Xiaowang had raised a problem for Ling Ran to solve. He could even be said to have pointed Ling Ran in the right direction.
*Ding*
This was when the system’s notification appeared.
[Mission: The Way Forward]
[Mission Details: Complete 50 abdominal surgeries where the patients’ recovery time is less than 60 hours]
[Mission Reward: Intermediate Treasure Chest]
Ling Ran’s eyebrows scrunched up.

Since the mission was only limited to abdominal surgeries, the only abdominal surgeries he knew how to perform were hepatectomy, cholecystectomy, splenectomy, and appendectomy. Moreover, orchiectomy was probably not included.

Out of these abdominal surgeries, it would be impossible for a patient who underwent hepatectomy to recover within 60 hours. A hepatectomy would be considered successful if the patient did not die within three days of the surgery, and it was perfectly normal for a patient to only be transferred out of the ICU three days after hepatectomy.

However, there was a slim chance that this would be possible with emergency splenectomy. This was especially true when the patient was relatively young, as they often recovered well from emergency surgeries. However, it would be a little bit of a fairytale for a patient to be able to recover in sixty hours after undergoing a splenectomy.
Hence, the only surgical methods that were suitable for Ling Ran when it came to completing this mission was cholecystectomy and appendectomy.
“We have to pay attention to his postsurgical care too,” Zuo Cidian said, “Good postsurgical care is important for a fast recovery.”
“We’ll have to tell the anesthetist to put in extra effort too.” Lu Wenbin offered his suggestion too.
“Should we also aim to use the best surgical instruments and medical consumables?” Ma Yanlin licked his pale lips with his pale tongue and suggested feebly.
Ling Ran nodded and said to Zuo Cidian, “Note all this down, and we’ll figure out a way to go about it.”

Huo Congjun became interested in the matter too when he heard this. “If you guys are really doing this, you can advertise yourself using the promise of fast recovery time. Hmm... since the patient is an employee in an internet company, he should be pretty rich, shouldn’t he?”

Zuo Cidian understood what Huo Congjun was implying, and he immediately said, “He’s definitely richer than us. Their insurance coverage is excellent too. Moreover, since they’re so busy racing against time, they probably receive excellent financial compensation.”

Huo Congjun nodded in agreement. “If the patient were an idiot who has no time and no money, there would be no need for him to strive for fast recovery time, right? Since he’s making this request because of the situation in his company, there should be many similar cases among his colleagues, shouldn’t it?”

“From what I heard from the patient, he has many colleagues with similar problems. There should be a lot of patients who are receiving conservative treatment for appendicitis, colitis, and cholecystitis...” Zuo Cidian combed his hair with his finger as he supported Huo Congjun’s statement.

As expected, Huo Congjun nodded and said, “Then, let’s start a project team and go about it as though it’s a research project. Doctor Zuo, go ahead and do the paperwork. I’ll allocate some funds for you guys.”
All of the doctors in the Ling Treatment Group nodded. The expressions of the other doctors in the office did not change, as though they did not hear anything.

sentences.text: Ling Ran first drew the anatomical structures of Chen Xiaowang’s abdominal cavity on a piece of paper based on the information he had obtained from the Virtual Human along with the examination results.
For surgeons, cholecystectomy was mainly difficult due to the variations in the structures of patients’ cystic artery and bile ducts.

The variation was so great that if a person were to categorize humans based on the differences in the structures of their gallbladder arteries and bile ducts, the list might be so long that it could not even fit into a book.
Naturally, Chen Xiaowang’s cystic artery and bile duct varied from those of other humans too.
There was a very obvious abnormality to his cystic artery, as it branched out very early into two arteries.
This condition was known as a double cystic artery.
This was considered a very normal abnormality, and tens of thousands of people might exhibit the same abnormality.
If the person did not receive surgery related to the gallbladder or bile duct, this abnormality would not be obvious at all.
It neither caused any discomfort nor affected a person’s health.
It would not even affect the organs around it to a significant extent.
It could be said to be even more insignificant than neighborhood committees outside Beijing.
However, if doctors failed to pay attention to this abnormality during cholecystectomy, it could easily lead to problems.
To prevent bleeding, during cholecystectomy, doctors had to first interrupt the blood flow of the cystic artery.
As ordinary people only had one cystic artery, doctors just need to clamp their cystic arteries with a hemostatic forceps.
However, in cases of patients with double cystic arteries, doctors may make a mistake and only interrupt the blood flow of the first cystic artery.
And when this happened, the second cystic artery was almost guaranteed to be accidentally damaged during the process of the surgery.
Major hemorrhage was almost a certainty, and a good prognosis would become impossible.
“Double cystic artery!” Ling Ran rose and wrote this down on the whiteboard in his office.
Not only did this serve as a reminder for himself, but also for other doctors to take note of.

Accidental damage sometimes happened because the chief surgeon made a mistake, but there were times when it happened because the chief surgeon did not manage his subordinates well by forgetting to give them a reminder.
“Edema in the gallbladder, and there’s inflammation.”
“The bile duct enters the hepatic duct after running parallel to the hepatic duct for a distance.”
As Ling Ran wrote on the whiteboard, he drew simple diagrams every now and then.
The ability to draw anatomical diagrams were essential to doctors, so it was only natural that other doctors were able to understand what Ling Ran was trying to convey.
Not only did the doctors in the Ling Treatment Group understand it, but doctors from other treatment groups were also sizing up the whiteboard in curiosity.
“Chronic cholecystitis, and the gallbladder has shrunk a little.
These aren’t really a problem.
The most difficult part is that the patient can only afford a recovery time of two and a half days.”
“I really don’t believe that companies nowadays overwork people to this extent.”
“Employers of companies have to make a living, right?
As doctors, even though we are super tired after working day and night, we still carry out freelance surgery during the weekends.
Why are we doing all these?”
“Some people chase after money, and some chase after their dreams.
Some chase both at the same time.
Truth be told, this has nothing to do with us.
From what I know, whenever Huawei executes a project, they aim to be two years ahead of their peers.
If their employers were to take short breaks, those breaks would accumulate over the course of time into a long period of time.
Then, wouldn’t their predecessor’s hard work to race against time become a waste?”
“But they should still have their basic rest time, shouldn’t they?”
“Basic rest time?

I don’t know how you were like as a student, but from I know, all the students who abide by the basic rest time either have no problem scoring 985 marks in their college entrance examination at all or can’t even pass after their second try.
Which type are you?”
Right after someone talked about school, the doctors’ office in the Emergency Medical Center immediately became a lot livelier.
Huo Congjun slowly walked over to Ling Ran and asked, “Have you made your decision?”
“Yes,” Ling Ran said.
As Huo Congjun looked at the diagrams that Ling Ran drew on the whiteboard, he shook his head and said, “Why would you trouble yourself over this?
There are so many patients waiting for you to operate on them.
Why don’t you just pass this case over to an ordinary doctor?
Moreover, truth be told, isn’t the patient’s request to recover in a span of two and a half days a little too much?”
Ling Ran said, “It’s also an opportunity for self-improvement.”
Huo Congjun asked in surprise, “What do you mean?”

“Improving patients’ prognoses and shortening the recovery time can be seen as an area of improvement when it comes to cholecystectomy.” Ling Ran was actually speculating that this was the way to elevate his cholecystectomy skills from Specialist Level to Master Level.
Unlike the other skills he possessed, Ling Ran learned cholecystectomy from scratch.
Now that he had gone from Novice Level to Specialist Level, Ling Ran did not actually have many ideas as to how to go forward.
Cholecystectomy in itself was a relatively simple surgery, especially when it was done using a laparoscope, and most doctors could complete it without any issue.
Even though doctors always strived to reduce damage and improve accuracy, all of this often felt a little vague, and it was not a true indicator of improvements in skills.
Without a doctor who was better at cholecystectomy to guide him, Ling Ran did not know how to improve further.
Without realizing it, Chen Xiaowang had raised a problem for Ling Ran to solve.
He could even be said to have pointed Ling Ran in the right direction.
*Ding*
This was when the system’s notification appeared.
[Mission: The Way Forward]
[Mission Details: Complete 50 abdominal surgeries where the patients’ recovery time is less than 60 hours]
[Mission Reward: Intermediate Treasure Chest]
Ling Ran’s eyebrows scrunched up.
Since the mission was only limited to abdominal surgeries, the only abdominal surgeries he knew how to perform were hepatectomy, cholecystectomy, splenectomy, and appendectomy.
Moreover, orchiectomy was probably not included.
Out of these abdominal surgeries, it would be impossible for a patient who underwent hepatectomy to recover within 60 hours.

A hepatectomy would be considered successful if the patient did not die within three days of the surgery, and it was perfectly normal for a patient to only be transferred out of the ICU three days after hepatectomy.
However, there was a slim chance that this would be possible with emergency splenectomy.
This was especially true when the patient was relatively young, as they often recovered well from emergency surgeries.
However, it would be a little bit of a fairytale for a patient to be able to recover in sixty hours after undergoing a splenectomy.
Hence, the only surgical methods that were suitable for Ling Ran when it came to completing this mission was cholecystectomy and appendectomy.

“We’ll have to tell the anesthetist to put in extra effort too.” Lu Wenbin offered his suggestion too.
“Should we also aim to use the best surgical instruments and medical consumables?” Ma Yanlin licked his pale lips with his pale tongue and suggested feebly.
Ling Ran nodded and said to Zuo Cidian, “Note all this down, and we’ll figure out a way to go about it.”

chapters.title: Chapter 784: Understand
paragraphs: “According to research papers, it is extremely effective to separate adhered tissues using electrocoagulation hooks and suction machines along with ultrasonic knives. However, ultrasonic knives are relatively expensive,” Yu Yuan voiced out during the preoperative consultation. Her back was straight, and she was practically sitting on her lumbar pillow so that she was at least visible from the neck up.
Ling Ran nodded. “Let’s use an ultrasonic knife, then. Doctor Zuo, remember to inform the patient about this.”

“We’ll have to submit a report to the Medical Affairs Department, as this will be considered usage of instruments beyond normal operation.” Zuo Cidian knew how the hospital worked well. He then continued, “Doctor Ling, you’ll have to talk to them to make sure that we get to use a new blade.”
“Sure,” Ling Ran said in acknowledgment.

Endotherm knives were used in ordinary cholecystectomy to reduce the cost of the surgery. It was a little more troublesome compared to ultrasound knives due to reasons such as the thermal effect. Hence, the prognosis would not be as good.

However, according to Yun Hua Hospital’s policies, surgeons were not allowed to simply increase the standard of the instruments used. In other words, surgeons should not strive to use the best instruments, but the ones that offered the best outcome among the cheap ones.
However, an ultrasound knife would be useful as it would reduce damage to a great extent.
Zuo Cidian wrote something down in his notebook and said, “I suggest that we used imported titanium clips too. This way, the patient will basically be funding all the instruments himself.”

Lu Wenbin twisted his mouth and said, “He’s in a company where he has to work more than ten hours a day six days a week, excluding overtime. If he didn’t make enough money to fund his own surgery, it would be a joke.”
Yu Yuan said calmly, “This is also the working hours of doctors. How many doctors make enough money to fund their own surgeries?”
“It’s only tens of thousands of RMB. When illnesses strike, every doctor would be able to come out with this sum of money.” Lu Wenbin snorted a few times.

Zhang Anmin chuckled. “I would rather use whatever is covered by my medical insurance and lie in the hospital bed for a few more days... Ah... One week would do too. I don’t mind staying in the hospital bed, urinate through a catheter and eating through a nasogastric tube. I will sleep until the world ends.”
He yawned as he spoke as if he was drugged.

Affected by him, Su Jiafu the anesthetist who had not said anything yet started yawning too. Next, Lu Wenbin and Ma Yanlin yawned too, and it was as if all of them were in a competition to see who could open their mouths the widest.
“Hm... this is a problem too. Should we get a day or half a day of rest before the surgery?” Zuo Cidian took the opportunity to raise a request. Truth be told, he would like to rest too.
Ling Ran thought about it for a moment and said, “This new project is a long-term one...”
From everyone’s expressions, they seemed to understand this fact.
Right after that, Ling Ran said, “In the beginning stages of the project, the doctors can take a day of rest. All the doctors participating in this surgery can go home and take a good rest at night.”
Zhang Anmin who had a mocking expression on his face immediately froze. “Rest for a day? Isn’t this a little too much?”
As he was still under the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, he was not able to take part in the first surgery of this project.
Even though Ma Yanlin was part of it, his gaze froze too. “We’re allowed to go home for a day?”
Ling Ran nodded. “Twenty-four hours. Doctor Zuo, do make a new schedule so that the doctors participating in the surgery can get a rest.”
Zhang Anmin was so envious that he almost salivated. He quickly raised his hand and said, “Doctor Ling, I would like to apply to participate in the next similar surgery.”
“Sure.” Ling Ran nodded.
Zuo Cidian took down some notes and asked, “Doctor Ling, will the doctors get to rest before the next surgery too?”
“No,” Ling Ran said without hesitation. “Cholecystectomy is still a routine surgery.”
“Okay, I understand.” There was a smile on Zuo Cidian’s wrinkly face as he looked at Zhang Anmin, and he looked extremely kindly.

They talked for a while about the details of the surgery and things they had to take note of. After talking about the patient’s post-surgical care and matters related to anesthesia, everyone left the meeting room speedily with their documents in their hands.

Since Ling Ran was officially back in the team, work immediately became strenuous for members of the Ling Treatment Group again. This was especially true after Ling Ran started offering consultation, as his treatment group was responsible for all the members he took in. In other words, the members of his treatment group got to share the patients.

Aside from acting as Ling Ran’s assistant and making daily ward rounds, Lu Wenbin also had the chance to act as chief surgeon for M-Tang surgeries that were not too complicated. Even though he did not often get this opportunity, if the time spent on preoperative preparation and postsurgical care was included, each patient might take up more than eight hours of his time. And Lu Wenbin did not have resident doctors to help him out. The most he could do was make housemen and medical interns write medical reports on his behalf.
Zhang Anmin was even busier.

Right now, Zhang Anmin was working in both the Emergency Medical Center and the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery. When it came to administrative work, Zhang Anmin had to answer to even more people compared to Ling Ran. Aside from this, he also had to carry out freelance surgery in Bazhaixiang. Hence, Zhang Anmin never got a moment of rest.

Even though the doctors of the Ling Treatment Group were able to get quite a lot of rest when Ling Ran was in Brazil, Zhang Anmin was even busier than usual. Zhang Anmin was a traitor of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, and right now, He Yuanzheng treated him like nothing but a piece of medical consumable and overworked him whenever possible.
Women who worked in the hospital were treated like men, while men who worked in the hospital were treated like animals. This was the custom. But there were various ways of enslaving animals.
A person definitely did not use the black ox they own the same way they do with their neighbor’s mule.

For the sake of extending his lifespan for a few days, Zhang Anmin went to Ma Yanlin with a piteous look on his face the moment he exited the meeting room. “Young Ma, we get along pretty well, right? You don’t seem that you are willing to have a long break either...”

“If you take three of my night shifts, I’ll let you rest tomorrow and take your place.” Ma Yanlin gazed at Zhang Anmin, and his brain was working hard to come up with ways to make the most out of this.
Zhang Anmin’s lips trembled. “Three night shifts are too many. How about two?”
“Lu Wenbin has already offered to take two of my night shifts.”
“Alright, three-night shifts it is, then!” Zhang Anmin agreed through gritted teeth, as it was quite a rare chance to get twenty-four hours of consecutive rest.
On Friday afternoon, at six, as agreed, Chen Xiaowang showed up at the Emergency Medical Center of Yun Hua Hospital. He barely made it on time.

“You’re certainly putting on quite the show of being busy! You’re the busiest patient that I’ve ever met. Seriously.” Ma Yanlin who had been on shift all day wore a slightly healthy complexion, and he was in the mood to tease Chen Xiaowang.

Chen Xiaowang explained helplessly. “I couldn’t help it. I told them that I would wrap up the day’s work at five, and I left ten minutes before that. Even though I’ll be absent for work, I had to get everything planned out beforehand.”
“Nothing’s easy in life.” Ma Yanlin smiled, and his youthful face was painted with fatigue.

“Sigh...” Chen Xiaowang sighed and followed Ma Yanlin to the ward for preoperative preparations. He then asked anxiously, “It won’t be a problem for me to only be able to rest for two and a half days, will it?”
“Sixty hours. As long as Doctor Ling is able to make it, you’ll be able to recover within that time frame.” Ma Yanlin did not make any promises.
Chen Xiao Wang lowered his head and watched as the nurse inserted a venous catheter into his vein for a fluid transfusion as well as did other things.
*Buzz*
Chen Xiaowang’s phone vibrated.
He whipped out his phone, took a look at it, and saw that one of his colleagues had messaged him to wish him good luck for the surgery.
Chen Xiaowang flashed a slight smile and casually composed a reply.
*Buzz, buzz*
His phone rang again, and it was a message from the same colleague. [If it’s possible, please take note of how the surgery goes, especially the state you’re in before and after the surgery.]

chapters.title: Chapter 785: Work Done Through Experience
paragraphs: *Beep... Beep...*
The monitor in the operating theater made a monotonous noise like a duck with a hand around its throat quacking while acting like a loan shark

Su Jiafu obediently sat on a round stool. From time to time, he looked at the numbers on the display screen and then looked at his department director carrying out his tasks like a duck with a hand around its throat hiding from loan sharks.

“Take propofol with remifentanil. You can reduce the dosage of propofol, this can also shorten your postoperative recovery time...” as the department director of the Department of Anesthesiology administered anesthesia, he also chatted a little with Su Jiafu.

Ling Ran was used to have Su Jiafu as his anesthetist, and both of them were able to cooperate with each other. But if they wanted to improve the patient’s prognosis in all aspects, especially in reducing the recovery time, a good anesthetist would be very important.
Su Jiafu was a good anesthetist, but he was still not skilled enough. He could only ask for his senior doctors in the Department of Anesthesiology for help when he wanted to improve even further.
After consulting the Department of Anesthesiology, they put forward the most suitable anesthetic plans and adopted venous anesthesia.

When compared to the commonly used sevoflurane for inhalation anesthesia throughout the entire surgery, remifentanil, which was commonly used in total intravenous anesthesia, provided a faster recovery rate, had a shorter effect on the patient, and prevented accumulation of substances in the patient’s body. When compared with the two groups, the probability of postoperative dementia was lower when using total intravenous anesthesia.

Postoperative dementia was a common complication after general anesthesia. Once it appeared, the patients’ cognitive ability, attention span, and language ability may have short-term impediments, and a few people may even have long-term impediments.

Of course, the probability of long-term impediment was very low, and postoperative dementia mainly occurred in elderly patients. In addition, the higher the patients’ education level, the lower the probability of postoperative dementia.

With Chen Xiaowang’s working environment, short-term dementia may already be something that he could not bear with. Once the department director of the Department of Anesthesiology was called on by Huo Congjun, even though he was not afraid of Huo Congjun, he still did not want Huo Congjun to look down on him. Hence, he considered many aspects when he chose his anesthesia plan.

A person who was despised by Huo Congjun would usually be scolded if he did something wrong, and Huo Congjun would even rebuke him while he looked down on him. As the director of the Department of Anesthesiology, he naturally could not go through such suffering.

The department director had been checking if the data on the display screen was stable before he watched Su Jiafu fill in the forms on the computer. He then pointed to the dosage of various drugs and said, “Next time you do the same thing, you need to have an idea of what’s going on. Don’t just make calculations blindly. Take cisatracurium besylate as an example. When you use it during induction, you have to control the amount used. When it comes to dexmedetomidine, pay more attention, if you used too much, the patient will have hypotension, bradycardia...”
Su Jiafu listened obediently like a trained puppy.
For Su Jiafu, who was a resident doctor, it was a rare opportunity to get training from the department director.

The Department of Anesthesiology was busier than ordinary specialist departments. If the doctors in other departments had reached the level of department directors, they would have some spare time for conversations. However, the department director of the Department of Anesthesiology had to often work on the front line.

As the saying went, “There are minor surgeries, but no minor anesthesia.” Once the department director of the Department of Anesthesiology had to work, he had to do things conscientiously, and he could not relax. That was why the new people in the department every year would be ignored by the department director unless someone asked for help.

It could be said that the growth of a doctor could not escape from coincidence. Two resident doctors might join the hospital at the same time, but they might receive teachings from two different doctors at two different levels, and it was a very metaphysical thing. Most of the time, it was not about the novices’ performances, but also about the senior doctors’ attitude and how busy they were.
Su Jiafu did not have the chance to listen to the department director’s lecture before, but now that he had this opportunity, he was naturally extremely grateful for it.
Similarly, Lu Wenbin and Ma Yanlin who were before the operating table also performed the surgery seriously.
They could all see that Ling Ran’s approach was very different today.

Surgeons were very crude when they performed surgeries. The more professional the doctors were, the cruder they would be sometimes. It was like taking care of a child. The parents would be more patient and worried more about their firstborn. They would feel nervous when they turn over and worry if they would end up squashing their arms. However, the parents’ attitude toward their second and third child would be absolutely different.
When general surgeons did their first appendectomy or their first cholecystectomy, they were absolutely afraid of making mistakes, but of course, they would definitely make mistakes.

However, during their tenth or twentieth case, some crude and illegal actions formed from habit would begin to appear. During the hundredth case, surgeons not only would form their own routines but also form their own unique, crude methods. They would be like a semi-new driver who had driven a car for two years. They would drive with the ferocity of a tiger, but if anyone looked closely, they would notice that these drivers were driving blindly.
In comparison, Ling Ran always had strict requirements, but not to the point of nitpicking.
After all, human bodies were different. It would be meaningless to emphasize a unified value or to be fixated on certain boundary lines.
But it seemed that Ling Ran’s requirements today were unusually high.
Even the output frequency of the ultrasonic knife was constantly adjusted, causing Lu Wenbin and Ma Yanlin could not understand what was going on, even though they were amazed by it.
Ling Ran was still silent. To be honest, he already said what he wanted to say during the preoperative consultation. All the maneuvers he currently performed had already been tried and tested.

An ultrasonic knife was a kind of medical device which could cut and solidify things using high-frequency vibration. To some extent, this kind of knife, which could reach over fifty thousand Hz at its highest frequency was the kind of technology that exceeded human understanding.
The greater the power output, the stronger the cutting ability. The lower the power output, the weaker the cutting ability, but it would have a stronger ability to coagulate and stop bleeding.
When the same doctor, used an ultrasonic knife for surgery, he would be one-third faster than when he used an endotherm knife for the surgery, and the effect would be better.
Besides, when performing bleeding control, an ultrasonic knife would be able to control the bleeding in one second, but an endotherm knife would take five seconds.
Since the endotherm knife would have longer contact with the tissues during those extra four seconds, it would just end up causing more damage.
Therefore, Ling Ran had to choose the right frequency and time to finish cutting and coagulating the blood without damaging the tissues.
Even the angle of the titanium clips had been specially adjusted and tested using the Virtual Human.

When the abdomen was closed, the bile duct and other tissues would be packed together. With the natural peristalsis of the body, when the titanium clips were not placed well, it would be easy for complications to arise.
However, these were all events that had a low probability of happening. If Chen Xiaowang had not made his request, there was no need for Ling Ran to be so meticulous.
But from another point of view, it was his request that gave Ling Ran a framework for his entire idea and a goal.

There was no specific data in many aspects of clinical medicine. In certain aspects, the surgeons were required to lower the power output of the ultrasonic knife, but how low was low? In certain aspects, the surgeons were required to be careful when they placed the titanium clamps, but just what angle were they striving for? There was no formula.
The value of surgeons was often reflected in this.
Surgeons’ experiences were accumulated through countless surgeries and contemplation. They also had to follow the right steps and do the right things. Over time, the success rate would increase.
In comparison, the development of evidence-based medicine was still new. It was still impossible to search for evidence in every step of the surgery.
But it was still possible for the surgeon to treat a patient and become even better based on the framework he used on the patient.
Maybe it would not change the world, but it would make the world a more hopeful and better place.

“Take propofol with remifentanil.

You can reduce the dosage of propofol, this can also shorten your postoperative recovery time...” as the department director of the Department of Anesthesiology administered anesthesia, he also chatted a little with Su Jiafu.
Ling Ran was used to have Su Jiafu as his anesthetist, and both of them were able to cooperate with each other.
But if they wanted to improve the patient’s prognosis in all aspects, especially in reducing the recovery time, a good anesthetist would be very important.
Su Jiafu was a good anesthetist, but he was still not skilled enough.
He could only ask for his senior doctors in the Department of Anesthesiology for help when he wanted to improve even further.
After consulting the Department of Anesthesiology, they put forward the most suitable anesthetic plans and adopted venous anesthesia.

When compared to the commonly used sevoflurane for inhalation anesthesia throughout the entire surgery, remifentanil, which was commonly used in total intravenous anesthesia, provided a faster recovery rate, had a shorter effect on the patient, and prevented accumulation of substances in the patient’s body.
When compared with the two groups, the probability of postoperative dementia was lower when using total intravenous anesthesia.
Postoperative dementia was a common complication after general anesthesia.
Once it appeared, the patients’ cognitive ability, attention span, and language ability may have short-term impediments, and a few people may even have long-term impediments.
Of course, the probability of long-term impediment was very low, and postoperative dementia mainly occurred in elderly patients.
In addition, the higher the patients’ education level, the lower the probability of postoperative dementia.
With Chen Xiaowang’s working environment, short-term dementia may already be something that he could not bear with.

A person who was despised by Huo Congjun would usually be scolded if he did something wrong, and Huo Congjun would even rebuke him while he looked down on him.

Don’t just make calculations blindly.
Take cisatracurium besylate as an example.
When you use it during induction, you have to control the amount used.
When it comes to dexmedetomidine, pay more attention, if you used too much, the patient will have hypotension, bradycardia...”

chapters.title: Chapter 786: Roll
paragraphs: Chen Xiaowang’s eyelids twitched a few times before he slowly opened his eyes. His eyes were glazed because of the long hours he spent in front of the computer every day, and he looked around for a short while. He then snorted a few times as he stared at the transfusion bag on his left.
“You’re awake.” Lu Wenbin immediately rose and glanced at the figures on the monitor.
“Cough, cough...” Chen Xiaowang’s throat felt a little uncomfortable, and it was hard for him to speak as his voice was extremely hoarse.
“The surgery went very well, there’s no need for you to worry. What are you trying to say?” Lu Wenbin lowered his head and brought his ear close to Chen Xiaowang’s mouth.
Chen Xiaowang said a little arduously, “Eyes...”
“Are you feeling discomfort in your eyes?”
Chen Xiaowang shook his head. “Glasses... or I can’t see anything.”

Lu Wenbin immediately understood. He nodded and said, “10.0 diopters, huh? Just wait for a while, and I’ll give you your glasses when we arrive at the ward. There’s no point in you having your glasses right now.”
“We’re not at the ward now?” Chen Xiaowang’s expression changed a little.

“We are in the recovery room.” Lu Wenbin pursed his lips and continued. “I’ll accompany you here for a while. Just let me know if you’re experiencing any discomfort. When you’re okay, we’ll transfer you to a normal ward.”
Chen Xiaowang took note of the sensations in his body and furrowed his eyebrows a little. “My wound seems to still be a little numb...”
“The effects of anesthetics have not waned completely yet,” Lu Wenbin explained. Even though he said that, he still rose and called Su Jiafu, the anesthetist over.
Su Jiafu quickly examined Chen Xiaowang and nodded. “There’s no problem. Old Lu, you can leave already.”
“Really?”
“If you don’t feel like leaving, ask someone to bring some pork trotters over. I’ll have dinner with you.” Su Jiafu chuckled.

“Exactly what I was thinking.” Unexpectedly, Lu Wenbin whipped out his phone for real and made a call. “Send two pork trotters over. Throw some braised intestines and braised bean curds along with two bowls of rice in too. Also, I want some soup. Send the food to the anesthetists’ office.”
Su Jiafu became happy when he heard that. “Not bad at all, Young Lu. You’re the boss now, aren’t you?”

“I would rather not be one.” Lu Wenbin shook his head. “You have no idea how troublesome it is to have employees. But there’s nothing I can do about it now since I’ve hired them, and they depend on me for a living. Sigh, if I knew that running this business would take up so much of my time, I would have just carried out freelance surgeries together with Doctor Ling. The pay wouldn’t be bad either... Let me tell you, when you’ve possessed a certain sum of money, money would be nothing but a number...”
Su Jiafu gazed at Lu Wenbin’s face. “If you ask the dude to send over some pork cheeks too, I’ll allow you to show off more.”

Lu Wenbin immediately whipped out his phone. He said as he typed something. “I just need to send a brief message when it comes to such a small matter. There’s no need for me to make a call. My subordinates are quite competent—”

Su Jiafu shook his head as he looked at Chen Xiaowang who had just regained consciousness. “Do you know why life is so difficult for anesthetists? It’s because we have to listen as surgeons show off all the time.”

By the time Chen Xiaowang was sent to the ward, he had basically regained his rationality. He was not asking for his glasses anymore either, as he felt that a blurry field of vision was more comforting. He did not have to look at the whiteboard at work with performance indicators written on it, his product manager who nagged people and changed his mind all the time, the heads of his bald colleagues, and his vast and desolate office...
“Old Chen, how do you feel?” A familiar voice rang out beside his ears.

Chen Xiaowang was surprised as he turned to look at the person speaking. “Old Piao? If you have the time, why aren’t you catching some sleep instead of visiting me? Aren’t you worried that you would drop dead?”
“I slept for a while in the car during my journey here, and also slept while I was waiting for you to regain consciousness.” Old Piao’s voice was nonchalant. He asked, “How do you feel?”
“Pretty good.”
“On a scale of one to ten, how do you feel?”
“Six.” Chen Xiaowang’s voice was weak, and he gave a one-word answer because he barely had any strength to speak.
“Hmm, so subjectively, you rate your overall condition six out of ten. How about your state of mind? Are you able to think clearly?”
Chen Xiaowang said hesitantly, “I should be able to.”
“One to ten?”
“Eight.”
“The kind of eight when you are drunk or the kind of eight after drinking coffee?”
Chen Xiaowang was confused for a few seconds. “You know, people always say that drunk people will never admit that they’re drunk. So, how can a person who’s not drunk prove that he’s not drunk?”

“Based on your ability to use your logical thinking right now, I don’t think that there’s much difference between you and a drunk person. Why don’t you try coding or solving math equations right now? Z short term is the best for this situation...” Old Piao chuckled as he whipped out two pieces of paper with words printed on them and passed them to Chen Xiaowang.
This was when a nurse who had been watching them could not take it anymore. “No, no! Are you trying to kill him by making him work right after his surgery?”
“This isn’t work-related...” Old Piao seemed like he was almost forty years old, but the nurse was scolding him as if he was her grandchild. His cheeks turned red.
Chen Xiaowang seemed to have come round. He gazed at Old Piao and said, “Are you treating me as a lab rat?”
Old Piao scratched his head a few times. “It’s not just me. All of us rolled a dice together, and unfortunately, I lost, so I came over.”
Chen Xiaowang no longer felt like saying anything.
Old Piao lowered his head and sighed. “Just complete this and summarize your experience. If your recovery goes well, I’ll be next to receive surgery. So, I’m naturally concerned.”
Chen Xiaowang pursed his lips. “Is there any humanity in you guys?”

“It’s called rationality, bro. We’re just being rational. Truth be told, I’ve had appendicitis for two years. It keeps recurring, and there’s no improvement at all. My abdomen aches every time I have to work overtime, and it’s really time for me to receive an appendectomy. I’m afraid that I’ll get cancer if I don’t do this...” Old Piao fidgeted as he spoke. “So, you really need to buckle up and get well soon.”

“If I can recover just by buckling up, my cholecystitis would have been cured a long time ago.” Chen Xiaowang snorted. He felt rather tired, so he closed his eyes as he spoke. “You should have made a cognitive ability test and asked me questions instead. That would have cut it. Why the heck did you make a math test. Are you crazy!?”

“Hehe, you’re right. Then, I’ll have to amend this a little. I’ll change things up and remake the test. Should I use a simple factory pattern?” Old Piao tapped his head and looked at his phone. “The day before yesterday, someone commented that he’ll be building a new framework. He even said that the comments must be written properly. Please write the comments properly, yeah?”
“This is too much.” Chen Xiaowang could not take it anymore. “Why don’t you just tabulate the data and analyze it? Why fret so much over it?”

“You’ve already received your surgery. It either went well or it didn’t. But how do we keep our cool? Let me tell you. If you’re unable to return to work in three days’ time, we won’t even be able to get our medical leave approved.”
Chen Xiaowang chuckled, but he somehow felt relaxed.
The surgery was over anyway, and there was no point in worrying about what happened next.

As Chen Xiaowang thought about this, he soon fell asleep again. When he woke up again, he saw that Old Piao was sitting on a chair in the ward and typing away on his laptop. The light from the laptop formed a halo around his face.
Chen Xiaowang could not help but smile. This was how things were like for programmers. They had to work day and night, and life was tremendously tiring for them...
“Bed 12, it’s time for us to check on you.” A few doctors in large white coats walked over to the door of the ward, and their voices were neither loud nor soft as they spoke.
Chen Xiaowang glanced at the window. He then looked at the doctors in astonishment. “You guys are making ward rounds in the middle of the night?”
“It’s morning now.” Lu Wenbin entered the ward and glanced at his clock. “It’s already three in the morning. Have you farted yet?”

chapters.title: Chapter 787: Just Get It Removed
paragraphs: “It looks good.”
“I’ll poke you a little. Do you feel pain?”

“Of course, I do!” Chen Xiaowang was so mad that he scolded his colleagues, but it just caused him to feel sore and in pain. Therefore, he quickly calmed down and laid down on his back, “Stop teasing me. In another nine hours, I’ll need to go to work. If my wound tears, I will scold you.”
The colleagues who surrounded the bed naturally ignored Chen Xiaowang. They still walked around while thinking about how to poke Chen Xiaowang to be sure of his condition.
Chen Xiaowang narrowed his eyes. He did not even watch the television, which was close to him. While he was on guard against his colleagues, he felt smug.

“Old Chen, you’re grinning so widely you look like the Joker. Did you put a knife to your own mouth, Old Chen?” Old Piao came again today. He recorded a few data and played in front of the bed. He looked at Chen Xiaowang and felt slightly envious.
Chen Xiaowang raised his head and chuckled. “Next time, I shall be called ‘illness-free person’. Those with sicknesses, don’t come close to me.”
Old Piao scoffed. “Let me list out the sicknesses you will get. Let’s go top to bottom, yeah? Hair loss, dry eye syndrome, rhinitis, pharyngitis, being a henpecked husband—”
“Hey, hey, you need to draw the baseline correctly. Look at your conscience and tell me, are these illnesses for a programmer? ”
Old Piao was speechless when he heard Chen Xiaowang’s words, and he found himself agreeing to him slightly.

“Now, it’s not considered slander if I call you a coward, right?” A programmer beside them joined the conversation. He raised his hand and said, “I’ll make a declaration here, I don’t have dry eye syndrome.”
“I don’t have it too. I only have trachoma.”
“I have conjunctivitis.” This person stared at Chen Xiaowang and asked, “How do you feel?”
“Quite good. I don’t feel anything special. I guess I’m in slight pain, but I can still stand it.” Chen Xiaowang described it in detail.
The programmer who mentioned that he had conjunctivitis thought for a few seconds before he turned around and quietly took out his phone.

Ten seconds later, the pink-eyed programmer shouted, “Bro, this is so unfair! Didn’t we agree to roll dice and get surgery one by one? Now all of you have taken leave? What about dice? Are we not rolling dice now?”
The programmers in the ward all laughed.
“Wei Kang, which day is your leave?” Old Piao took a glance around at the others and knew they had applied for leave in the company, just like him.

The company could still approve their two-and-a-half-day leave, where the weekend was included in the leave. Naturally, the company would not allow them to take leave en masse, even when there were a lot of people who wanted to apply for two-and-a-half-day leave, they needed to queue up.
And if they could not get it at the first batch, they might need to wait for the second week.
“I took this week.” Someone who queued up early was proud.
“I took next week.”
“I took next week too.”

The programmers in the ward basically queued up within the first and second weeks. There were not many people who wanted to do this since the beginning, anyway, and there were even fewer people who knew about the news.

“I really have conjunctivitis.” Wei Kang, who was the only one queuing on the third week, was so mad that he felt that his hair was about to fall off. “I’ve had enteritis for a few years. Hey, we gotta queue according to the severity of illness, right?”
“First come first serve.”

“There’s no talk about severity when a person is sick, you know? Is your enteritis more severe than my appendicitis? I need to remove the whole appendix to treat my appendicitis. If you dare remove your intestines, I will give up my place for you.”
“We’re still unsure of the outcome, so why are you fighting over each other now? What if Old Chen dies of complications tomorrow? What should we do if all of you take leave?”
The room was in a mess now, but it was also because everyone was too bored and too anxious.
Chen Xiaowang felt he was cursed, even though he was innocent, so he just smiled. “Did all of you ask Doctor Ling about what surgery he performs, and what surgery he doesn’t perform?”
When they heard this from him, the temperature in the room instantly dropped.
A few seconds later, Old Piao nodded slightly. “Hearing this from Old Chen makes me believe that his intelligence has recovered.”
“I think so too. His face is in a healthy shade of red as well, and he looks like he can work now.”
“We need to give him more work later.”

“Doctor Ling can perform appendectomy, cholecystectomy, hepatectomy, knee arthroplasty, Achilles tendon repair, finger replantation, treat bone fractures...” A young nurse hiding at the corner suddenly said, and the atmosphere in the room became cold once more. She said, “You have ten more minutes of visitation time in the special care unit.”

The special care unit was renovated from a normal ward. It contained two or three beds in a room, and there were nurses taking care of the patients at all times. The patients were given special care similar to the standards in the ICU, but the care they provided was not as complete as the ICU, and they did not have such high standards of protection like the ICU. Naturally, its price was much lower. In Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center, when patients with hepatectomy first came out from the ICU, they would be transferred into the special care unit for a few days before they were transferred into a normal ward.

Chen Xiaowang was sent into the special care unit, and it also meant that the nursing care he received was upgraded. In fact, since the nursing team was given to him, they had designed more plans for the perioperative period and arranged more manpower for it.
The patient’s family and colleagues would not offend the nurse. At this time, they were all smiling.

Someone asked in a show of concern, “What do you mean that he only performs appendectomy and the others that you mentioned? Is Doctor Ling not willing to treat other positions of the body or something else?”
“Have you ever heard of any doctor who can perform every surgery?” The young nurse cackled as if she was a cat laughing at her human slave.
All of them nodded as if they understood but did not want to understand.
“He doesn’t handle enteritis? Enteritis is similar to appendicitis. ” Wei Kang gnashed his teeth and looked like a husky who was beaten up.
“Doctor Ling doesn’t handle enteritis. ” The young nurse nodded confidently and said, “Enteritis is within the field of general surgery, you need to look for them.”
“They can’t even promise us a seven-day recovery.” Wei Kang pursed his lips.
The young nurse did not continue to speak. The recovery of intestines was more troublesome. If she said anything wrong, it would be very easy for others to complain about her.
“Please help us ask Doctor Ling about this. If I still don’t queue up, I’m scared that I may not be able to queue up ever again.” Wei Kang covered his tummy with his hands.

“Doctor Ling really doesn’t treat enteritis. If you’re really not okay, you should think of a way to take leave,” the young nurse said as she shook her head, “From what I know, the only other surgery Doctor Ling performed that I didn’t mention just now is hemorrhoid surgery, which he did in Brazil.”
“I also have hemorrhoids.” Wei Kang’s eyes lit up, but he began doubting himself in an instant. ‘What am I proud of?’
Old Piao chuckled. “That’s great, you can get your hemorrhoids treated as well, and you can have your worries settled.”
“What kind of hemorrhoids do you have? Mine is mixed hemorrhoids. I should be able to get it removed, right?”
“Remove it. It’d be the best to remove it all at once.”
The atmosphere in the room became agitated, and everyone was excited.
“Visiting hours are over. Patient’s family and colleagues, please leave.” The young nurse acted as if she took a look at her watch, then she chased out the group of hemorrhoids infected people.
The people were not bothered by her actions. But they did give their blessings to Chen Xiaowang when they were about to leave.
“Take care of yourself.”
“Tell us if you don’t feel well.”
“Sleep more today. Don’t play with your phone. Get well soon.”
Chen Xiaowang answered weakly. When they left, he complained to the young nurse, “Why didn’t you mention earlier that hemorrhoid surgery was available? I can just get it removed too.”

chapters.title: Chapter 788: Scan My Face
paragraphs: In the special care unit, Yu Yuan looked at the report with a serious face. From time to time, she would glance at the bed.
Chen Xiaowang and his family, who were sitting in front of the bed looked nervously at Yu Yuan as well as the report in her hand.
*Flip flip flip*
Yu Yuan turned the report page by page.
Chen Xiaowang and his family’s hearts thumped loudly against their chests, but if their hearts did not beat... they would be dead.
“Doctor? How is it?” Chen Xiaowang’s father was nervous. He thought that his son’s company was good, but it would be awful if he lost his job because of physical discomfort.

Yu Yuan put away the report, looked up at the Chen family, and said, “The patient can be discharged from the hospital, but my suggestion is that it’s better for him to go home and rest. Do not start work immediately, and absolutely do not work overtime.”
Chen Xiaowang shook his head. “I have to go to work.”
Yu Yuan gave him a final piece of advice. “There is no need to work so hard. As family members, you should also advise him not to. The world can still go on with or without anyone.”
“That’s what I’m afraid of.” Chen Xiaowang sighed.
Father Chen asked, “Can he go to work? Can his body hold up? Doctor?”

“The recovery period of two and a half days is too short.” Yu Yuan paused for a moment before she said, “Short-term work should be possible, but you have to pay attention to your body at all times and still have to rest more.”
Once she said this, Yu Yuan did not say much anymore. In fact, if it were not an experimental project, she should not be saying these things.
Chen Xiaowang naturally nodded again and again. As long as he could go to work, he would even kneel down, so nodding was nothing to him.
Yu Yuan wrote a discharge form and turned around to pass it to Chen Xiaowang.
However, Chen Xiaowang could not even wait for even one more minute. He quickly said, “Dad, go through the formalities, I’ll go to the company to work first. The team is waiting...”
Father Chen unwillingly shook his head. “It’s not like you’re hurrying for reincarnation... Ack, what am I saying...”

Chen Xiaowang could not care more and hurried away. He had not been to work for two and a half days, and who knew how much work he had accumulated. If he did not go sooner, the new tasks for the day would just continue piling up on his already existing workload.
Yu Yuan continued her ward rounds. Today, she deliberately visited Chen Xiaowang first and completed his discharge procedures before proceeding to inspect the other patients.

Ling Ran had just returned recently. He had only performed over twenty hepatectomies even after working overtime. That was the workload for a normal doctor over one or two months. For Ling Ran’s current treatment group, this was nothing. The doctors in charge postponed the postoperative patient’s ward rounds till dawn. As for the preoperative patients, there was no other way to go about it. Ling Ran’s treatment group was not the only group to wake up the preoperative patients at three or four o’clock in the morning, this was something that also happened often in the other departments in Yun Hua Hospital.

At present, Yu Yuan only had ten beds under her charge, and if she counted the extra beds, she usually would not have a number of more than twenty-five beds under her care. It was comparable to other hospital’s ordinary resident doctors, and it was the least among many resident doctors in Ling Ran’s treatment group.

This was also because she was a chief resident. According to Yun Hua Hospital’s system, chief residents always had to perform a large number of operations to improve their skills and prepare to be an attending physician. Correspondingly, the number of beds they were in charge of was reduced. For Ling Ran’s treatment group, that meant ten beds, with a maximum of twenty-five beds, and this was considered light. Yu Yuan was also indeed not busy. As long as the person had no personal life and was living in the hospital, even if they had to care for the full workload of twenty-five beds, they could still fully inspect all patients in their free time.
Yu Yuan did not plan to pursue a personal life now.
Chief residents in any hospital always had no personal life, but Yu Yuan had been tirelessly trying to be a chief resident for several years.

To be honest, if she did not want to be a surgeon from the beginning to the end of her career, Yu Yuan would have long since resigned and put up with the Department of Internal Medicine, which was not only relaxing, but it would also allow her to better use her talents.

The atmosphere in the Department of Internal Medicine was much better than in the Department of Surgery. The Department of Surgery used a master-apprentice model. The senior doctor was the junior doctor’s father, and the only reason why the senior doctors did not deal physical punishment as discipline for the junior doctors in a show of fatherly love was already a sign of the advancement of times and the spark of civilization. But in the Department of Internal Medicine, because one could make progress by reading literature and providing thoughts on case studies, young doctors were far less oppressed than those in the Department of Surgery. Before the implementation of the separation of fees between the prescription of medicine and consultation, the Department of Internal Medicine earned more than the Department of Surgery. In general, medical students five years ago who went to the hospital and chose to join the Department of Surgery were either passionate or stupid if they were not affected by film and television works.
Yu Yuan was both passionate and stupid, so she did want to leave even if she had not had a good life in the Department of Surgery. Even if she was not welcome, she did not want to leave.

When she stepped into the operating area, changed into a surgical gown with thick linen, and felt the slight breeze of the operating theater, Yu Yuan could not help but show a smile, and that smile even resembled a bit like Ling Ran’s.
“Let me see the surgery timetable today.” Yu Yuan looked at the A4 paper attached to the wall, and she constantly weighed the pros and cons of the surgeries listed on the table.
She completed the ward rounds an hour earlier, so she had almost two hours of free time. During this time, she could see other people’s surgery when she did not have any to perform.
At a glance, Yu Yuan saw a small line: simple hemorrhoidectomy.

Yu Yuan then immediately went to see the names of the doctors who would be performing the operation, which were listed in the right column. She saw “Ling Ran” behind it, and “Ma Yanlin” was listed as the first assistant.
Yu Yuan’s eyebrows immediately rose, and as soon as her lower back tensed up, she ran to Operating Theater 4.
*Swish*
Yu Yuan stepped open the operation door vigorously. Before the airtight door was completely opened, she already went in at lightning speed.

“I knew it, Ma Yanlin, are you secretly performing the operation yourself?” Yu Yuan looked at Ling Ran, who stood behind Ma Yanlin with his arms crossed while he watched the operation, and then at Ma Yanlin. Her eyes almost spat fire.

“It’s only surgery, don’t get so worked up.” Ma Yanlin was a little scared. He used the fact that he was standing in the position of a chief surgeon to give himself courage and said, “Doctor Yu, we’ll go back and discuss anything that you want. We’re busy in the operating theater.”
Yu Yuan ignored him. She turned to Ling Ran and said, “Doctor Ling, I also want to learn hemorrhoid surgery!”

“Why do you want to learn hemorrhoid surgery?” Ling Ran gave Yu Yuan a puzzled look. For doctors, hemorrhoid surgery was dirty and had little technical content, and when compared to hepatectomy techniques, there was a huge gap in skill.

To describe it, hemorrhoid surgery was at most the level of a Four Tigers Door Breaker Saber Technique. It could not even be regarded as a branch of the Five Tigers Door Breaker Saber Technique. Hepatectomy was equivalent to the seventy-two ultimate techniques of Shaolin. If learned well, a doctor could conquer the world with it.
However, Yu Yuan’s pursuits were obviously not the technique itself. She saw Ma Yanlin’s actions and said, “I want to do it, Doctor Ling, please teach me.”
Both Ling Ran and Ma Yanlin looked at Yu Yuan.
Ma Yanlin said in displeasure, “It’s only a hemorrhoid surgery, and you still want to learn it?”
Yu Yuan blushed and frowned while she said, “In case I resign, I will need to go to a private hospital.”
“Well, the difficulty of hemorrhoid surgery is not high.” Ling Ran agreed, and from his point of view, Yu Yuan was indeed not suitable for surgery that was too technically difficult.

“I’m going to wash my hands.” Yu Yuan went out at her fastest speed before she came back. She stood beside Ma Yanlin, replacing the position of an unnamed intern, and became Ma Yanlin’s first assistant.
“Ah, there aren’t many patients with this disease, though.” Ma Yanlin sighed.
Yu Yuan snorted and said, “Weren’t all the patients from the company that would only allow its employees two and a half days off diagnosed with hemorrhoids? This one is also the same, right?”
“I am...” The patient who was lying on the operating table replied sullenly.

Yun Hua Hospital was a tertiary Grade A hospital in the region. Even if it was the Colorectal Department, they were also short on ward beds. They would only receive patients with hemorrhoid surgery for a while before they stopped taking them in, then went back to receiving them. The Emergency Department had no other place to get resources for these patients, and normal hemorrhoid patients would not run to the Emergency Department to see a doctor. So Yu Yuan’s guess was absolutely correct with her guess.
Ma Yanlin scoffed. “Only companies that give their employees only two and a half days off would have their employees have such a disease.”
“For hemorrhoid surgery, two and a half days of rest time would not be enough.” Yu Yuan looked at Ma Yanlin with a look of contempt. He was just an authorized houseman, anyway.
I’m working in the mobile terminal field. I’m not too busy lately, so I’m allowed to take annual leave...” The patient tried his best to participate in the conversation.
Yu Yuan acknowledged with an ‘okay’ and suddenly said, “What a coincidence. My phone has been lagging pretty badly lately, can you help me take a look at it? It’s in my left pocket.”
The circulating nurse then took out the mobile phone in Yu Yuan’s left pocket and gave it to the patient lying on the operating table.
The patient looked at the phone and could not help but start pondering.
“You can’t unlock it? Scan my face.” Yu Yuan shoved her face forward.

“I knew it, Ma Yanlin, are you secretly performing the operation yourself?” Yu Yuan looked at Ling Ran, who stood behind Ma Yanlin with his arms crossed while he watched the operation, and then at Ma Yanlin.
Her eyes almost spat fire.
“It’s only surgery, don’t get so worked up.” Ma Yanlin was a little scared.
He used the fact that he was standing in the position of a chief surgeon to give himself courage and said, “Doctor Yu, we’ll go back and discuss anything that you want.
We’re busy in the operating theater.”
Yu Yuan ignored him.
She turned to Ling Ran and said, “Doctor Ling, I also want to learn hemorrhoid surgery!”
“Why do you want to learn hemorrhoid surgery?” Ling Ran gave Yu Yuan a puzzled look.
For doctors, hemorrhoid surgery was dirty and had little technical content, and when compared to hepatectomy techniques, there was a huge gap in skill.
To describe it, hemorrhoid surgery was at most the level of a Four Tigers Door Breaker Saber Technique.
It could not even be regarded as a branch of the Five Tigers Door Breaker Saber Technique.
Hepatectomy was equivalent to the seventy-two ultimate techniques of Shaolin.
If learned well, a doctor could conquer the world with it.
However, Yu Yuan’s pursuits were obviously not the technique itself.
She saw Ma Yanlin’s actions and said, “I want to do it, Doctor Ling, please teach me.”
Both Ling Ran and Ma Yanlin looked at Yu Yuan.
Ma Yanlin said in displeasure, “It’s only a hemorrhoid surgery, and you still want to learn it?”
Yu Yuan blushed and frowned while she said, “In case I resign, I will need to go to a private hospital.”
“Well, the difficulty of hemorrhoid surgery is not high.” Ling Ran agreed, and from his point of view, Yu Yuan was indeed not suitable for surgery that was too technically difficult.
“I’m going to wash my hands.” Yu Yuan went out at her fastest speed before she came back.
She stood beside Ma Yanlin, replacing the position of an unnamed intern, and became Ma Yanlin’s first assistant.
“Ah, there aren’t many patients with this disease, though.” Ma Yanlin sighed.
Yu Yuan snorted and said, “Weren’t all the patients from the company that would only allow its employees two and a half days off diagnosed with hemorrhoids?
This one is also the same, right?”
“I am...” The patient who was lying on the operating table replied sullenly.
Yun Hua Hospital was a tertiary Grade A hospital in the region.
Even if it was the Colorectal Department, they were also short on ward beds.
They would only receive patients with hemorrhoid surgery for a while before they stopped taking them in, then went back to receiving them.
The Emergency Department had no other place to get resources for these patients, and normal hemorrhoid patients would not run to the Emergency Department to see a doctor.
So Yu Yuan’s guess was absolutely correct with her guess.
Ma Yanlin scoffed.
“Only companies that give their employees only two and a half days off would have their employees have such a disease.”
“For hemorrhoid surgery, two and a half days of rest time would not be enough.” Yu Yuan looked at Ma Yanlin with a look of contempt.
He was just an authorized houseman, anyway.
I’m working in the mobile terminal field.
I’m not too busy lately, so I’m allowed to take annual leave...” The patient tried his best to participate in the conversation.
Yu Yuan acknowledged with an ‘okay’ and suddenly said, “What a coincidence.
My phone has been lagging pretty badly lately, can you help me take a look at it?
It’s in my left pocket.”
The circulating nurse then took out the mobile phone in Yu Yuan’s left pocket and gave it to the patient lying on the operating table.
The patient looked at the phone and could not help but start pondering.
“You can’t unlock it?
Scan my face.” Yu Yuan shoved her face forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 789: Improved
paragraphs: At noon, the sun’s rays felt pretty hot on the skin, and it shone so violently on the leaves of the devil’s ivy that they curled up slightly.
Under the window where the devil’s ivy was placed, Yu Yuan happily enjoyed her braised pork trotter with rice while she recalled every specific detail of the surgical process in her mind.

After she thought long enough, Yu Yuan could not help but share with Ma Yanlin, who was beside her. “Although Doctor Ling feels that the difficulty level of hemorrhoid surgery is low, I think that there are actually still many areas to be studied, just like how many people have researched the resting pressure for the anal canal. Also, if we go into external hemorrhoid dissection and external hemorrhoidectomy in detail...”
“Can we not talk about this now?” Ma Yanlin looked at the pork cheeks on his plate and reconstructed his psychology before he could continue eating again.
The freshly cooked pork cheeks were braised with stew. They were not only savory but also tender and pulpy like feces. When Ma Yanlin thought of the term “feces”, his desire to eat was reduced again.
Yu Yuan was similarly unhappy and said, “Later, we have to perform surgery again. If we don’t discuss it now, we won’t improve in the surgery in the afternoon.”
“I think I’ve improved.” Ma Yanlin put down the chopsticks and said deliberately, “I can now be the chief surgeon for hemorrhoid surgery independently.”
Yu Yuan snorted. “Whether you can be the chief surgeon independently or not depends on Doctor Ling. If I’m not there, you can’t do it too.”

“Yes, you’re right.” Ma Yanlin was forced to admit. He was a houseman, so theoretically, doctors who had not obtained their medical practitioner qualification certificate were not qualified to perform surgery, much less become a chief surgeon.

However, there was a slight leeway in the rules. Theoretically, as long as the houseman was accompanied by a qualified doctor, he could still perform the surgery, just like how a new driver was not allowed to drive on the highway in a year, but if he were accompanied by an experienced driver, he could still drive the car on the road.

When Yu Yuan and Ma Yanlin performed hemorrhoid surgery, the real chief surgeon was Ma Yanlin, but Yu Yuan was the one who signed the form as the chief surgeon, and this was pretty common among the hospitals in China.

Most of the senior doctors also did not oppose this. Firstly, the person who signed up as chief surgeon would have the surgery fee paid to his bank card. Second, this was also one of the benefits that the senior doctors gave to junior doctors, which was an act that did not cost much.
Yu Yuan was a special case. She really wanted to be the chief surgeon, not just sign it and be the assistant.

“I want to be the chief surgeon.” Yu Yuan looked at Ma Yanlin and said, “If I can’t, I’d rather go to the emergency room and wait for patients or write papers in the office. Both are still more interesting than being an assistant for hemorrhoid surgery.”
“Are you still not happy with earning money from such an easy task?”
“You can ask whoever seems happy with this from the department to sign the form for you.” Yu Yuan casually threatened him.

Ma Yanlin could not retort. Doctors who were below at positions below an assistant lecturer performed surgeries to increase their experience, and they treated each surgery with great value. If a certain surgery did not allow them to gain experience or was one they were not interested in, they would naturally stay far away from it.
When senior doctors required them to do the surgery, they would do it if they could not avoid it, and a houseman like Ma Yanlin was someone they could order around as they liked.
For the configuration of Ling Ran’s treatment group, Ma Yanlin could really not find a doctor who was willing to accompany him for hemorrhoid surgery except Yu Yuan.

Ling Ran’s treatment group was different from other treatment groups. Other treatment groups had doctors who could not perform surgeries and could not even fill up their own stomachs, but under Ling Ran, all doctors had to work at full capacity.
Even if one or a few doctors were not exhausted at all times, they also dared not toy with their own lives, because they needed to keep their energy to work under Ling Ran until they die of fatigue.

Because of his status as a houseman, Ma Yanlin did not have the opportunity to be a chief surgeon. When he finally met a company that only offered two and a half days off for its company, he used the fact that he was young and operated on a few employees who worked for more than ten hours six days a week in the administration and logistics department, but once he finished going through this batch, the remaining employers who worked twenty-four hours per day seven days per week would definitely not land in his hands.
Yu Yuan... Without Yu Yuan, the chief resident, Ma Yanlin would also not have the chance to be the chief surgeon.
After all, it was impossible for Ling Ran to accompany him all the time and watch him perform hemorrhoid surgery.

“Then, you need to watch me for the surgery first.” Ma Yanlin glanced at Yu Yuan. He dared not immediately give away the position of the chief surgeon to her. Also, if he gave away the position, what else could he play with?

“Go on with it, then. Talk while doing the surgery, and teach seriously.” Yu Yuan snorted. She could actually perform quite a number of emergency surgeries now, especially foreign body removal surgeries. Yu Yuan was the doctor who performed this sort of surgery the most in the Emergency Medical Center.
After all, she was just less talented. If a doctor needed to do eight to ten surgeries to get a handle of a basic surgical method, Yu Yuan might need to practice for more than twenty times.
However, diligence was the means by which one made up for flaws, and this was true. For top doctors, both talent and hard work were required. However, most of the doctors could not reach the top.
The majority of them could not even be considered very hardworking, so they could only become a member of a normal treatment group.
Besides, most regular people would only be struck by general diseases, so similarly, they did not need top-tier doctors to treat them.
Ma Yanlin’s surgery talent was slightly better than Yu Yuan, but he was not that much better. After all, his physical talents did not lie in his hands.
Ma Yanlin also agreed with Yu Yuan’s request and said, “I will not hide anything, but you need to practice and get permission from Doctor Ling before you can really be the chief surgeon.”
Ma Yanlin guessed that when Yu Yuan became the chief surgeon, he would not have anything to do, so he deliberately emphasized this point to try to drag out the inevitable moment.
“Perform three more surgeries, then let me try half of one surgery. If my skills are alright, I’ll look for Doctor Ling.”
“At least seven or eight surgeries.”
“Five surgeries, if you’re not willing to, I’ll go to the emergency room.”
“Okay, deal.” Ma Yanlin helplessly agreed with her.
Yu Yuan showed a smile, then she stirred her braised pork trotter with rice again.

The intern beside Yu Yuan quietly gave a thumbs up to Ma Yanlin. Compared to the serious little leopard, Yu Yuan the chief resident, who checked through medical cases like she was checking through homework, the new intern thought Houseman Ma Yanlin was friendlier.
“Young Ma, are you having lunch with interns?” Department Director Lei from the Medical Affairs Department smiled and appeared in front of the table.
Ma Yanlin was a little stunned, but he immediately stood up and greeted Department Director Lei. “Department Director Lei, Doctor Yu and I have just finished surgery.”

Department Director Lei only just noticed Yu Yuan, who was by the side, so he quickly waved at her so that she did not feel neglected. “Alright. Good, even when you’re back, you still have to work hard like the doctors in our hospital. Yu Yuan too.”
Ma Yanlin was totally confused. ‘Do some of the doctors in our hospital have this kind of personality? Don’t all of them usually work hard in earning money?’
Yu Yuan stared ahead without any emotions. This was what she achieved after many years of practice.

Department Director Lei coughed and said, “Young Ma, you did a great job in Brazil this time, and I’ve also applied for you to be authorized here. Work hard in the future. Yes, Doctor Yu, you also did a good job, there should be a reward for you.”
Department Director Lei said as he nodded. Once he took the credit for this task, he turned around to leave.
Ma Yanlin was stunned for a while before he quickly swiped his phone. There were really private messages from his friends.
“Congratulations, you’ll be settled down in the Emergency Medical Center.” The internal news from Yun Hua Hospital always spread like a deluge, so it was expected that someone spread the news over.
Ma Yanlin quickly typed and expressed his gratitude before he asked, “Why do you say ‘settle down’?”
“Stop pretending. Your letter of appointment is already prepared for you. When you pass the medical licensing exam, you’ll be an official resident doctor.”
Ma Yanlin laughed out loud, put away his phone, looked at Yu Yuan, and showed a smile on his face. “Eight surgeries.”
